    NavButton

    NavButton extends UI Toolkit Button. Clicking it publishes a UI Button address to the active UINavigatorBehaviour.

    <nav:NavButton name="open-settings"
               text="Settings"
               signal-category="Menu"
               signal-key="OpenSettings" />
    Attribute Default Description
    signal-category Default Button catalog category
    signal-key Empty Button key within the category

    The combined address is available from the public Signal property. If either component is empty, clicking logs a [NavButton] warning and no event is sent.

    Connect it to the graph

    1. Add the address under the Button tab in Key Catalog.
    2. Select that address on NavButton in UI Builder.
    3. Choose + Add Output > UIButton on the relevant UI node, then assign the same address. The created port is displayed as UI Button. Alternatively, use the address as a UI Button Portal condition.
    4. Connect the output to one UI or Action chain.
    Important

    The property names contain signal, but this control does not emit the general Signal channel. A graph Signal output listens to UINavigationEvents.RequestSignal(...) and will not match a NavButton click.

    To publish the same event without a visual button, call:

    UINavigationEvents.RequestButtonSignal("Menu", "OpenSettings");

    Because NavButton inherits Button, standard attributes, USS selectors, focus behavior, and the clicked event remain available. The package also adds the ui-navigation-button USS class.
